sentences.text: Offences complained off U/s.498A and 307 of IPC Opinion of the Judge Accused found not guilty
JUDGMENT The Police Sub-Inspector, Rajagopalanagar P.S., Bangalore City, has filed charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable U/s.498-A and 307 of IPC in their crime No.18/2016.

2. The factual matrix of the case is that:-
About eight years back accused married-younger sister of informant by name Smt.
Meena, at Adichunchanagiri Temple, and after the marriage Smt. Meena started residing along with accused at House bearing No.26, situated at 2nd Cross, IP Nagar,
Laggere, within the limits of Rajagopalanagara P.S., Bangalore, prior to the marry Smt. Meena, accused obtained divorce from his first wife and working as Driver at Depot No.8 BMTC, and out of the wedlock accused and CW.8-Smt. Meena blessed with a child, and CW.8 doing the tailoring work at home, accused being the husband of CW.8 Smt.

Meena subjected her to physical and mental cruelty by suspecting her fidelity by assaulting and even after the advise accused continued to harass Cw.8, and on 6.1.2016 at 8.30 p.m. the accused with an intention and knowledge and on suspecting her fidelity attempted to kill her by stabbing over her chest with knife and thereby the accused has committed the offences as alleged against him.

3.The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the jurisdictional VII Addl., CMM.,
Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing charge sheet copy to the accused.
The same was numbered as SC No.510/2018.
4.The charge was framed and read over to the accused on 1.11.2022 for the offences punishable U/s.498A and 307 of IPC.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
5.The prosecution has examined in all three witnesses as PW.1 to PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P4.

In spite of sufficient opportunities provided, the prosecution has not taken any steps to secure the witnesses CW.2 to CW.7 and CW.9 to CW.13, in view of the same dropping of evidence of CW.2 to CW.7 and CW.9 to CW.13 remained intact.

The witnesses CW.2 to CW.7 and CW.9 to CW.13 have not been examined by the prosecution due to failure of concerned police to secure the said witnesses and keep present before the Court for the purpose of evidence.

So the evidence of prosecution was taken as closed with an opportunity to examine the said witness CW.2 to CW.7 and CW.9 to CW.13, if the said witnesses were secured and produced by the concerned police before the Court for examination before conclusion of the trial.
6.After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused on 7.3.2024 as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him, and not chosen to lead defense evidence.

sentences.text: 7.Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.

8.The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused being husband of victim-Smt. Meena while residing at House bearing No.26, situated at 2nd Cross, IP Nagar, Laggere, within the limits of Rajagopalanagara P.S.,
Bangalore,, subjected Smt.Meena to physical and mental cruelty and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.498-A of IPC ?
2.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused being husband of the victim-Smt. Meena while residing at House bearing No.26,
situated at 2nd Cross, IP Nagar, Laggere, within the limits of Rajagopalanagara P.S.,
Bangalore,, subjected Smt.Mena to physical and mental cruelty and on on 6.1.2016 at 8.30 p.m. the accused with an intention and knowledge and on suspecting her fidelity attempted to kill her by stabbing over chest with knife and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.307 of IPC?
3. What Order?
9.This Court findings on the above points are as hereunder:
Point No.1: In the Negative Point No.2: In the Negative Point No.3: As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Points No.1 and 2: Both the points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.
It is the case of the prosecution that bout eight years back accused married-younger sister of informant by name Smt. Meena, at Adichunchanagiri Temple, and after the marriage Smt. Meena started residing along with accused at House bearing No.26, situated at 2nd Cross, IP Nagar,

11.Among the 4 witnesses examined by the prosecution, the prime witness PW.1 Smt. Bhagya being the informant deposed that CW.8 Smt. K. B. entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In fact it was second marriage to the accused, the accused was working as Driver in BMTC.
They blessed with a daughter, now aged about 13 years.

Due to the matrimonial dispute between the accused and her sister K. B. Meena she have an oral complaint to the jurisdictional police, to advise the accused to lead happy married life with her sister.
Now the accused and CW.8 Smt. K. B. Meena leading their happy life with their daughter.
She did not allege against the accused that the accused is suspecting her sister Smt. Meena and attempted to stab her sister.
She does not know the contents of Ex.P1 complaint written by the concerned police.
She puts her signature on Ex.P2 mahazar in the police station.
Ex.P2 mahazar was not drawn in her presence.
PW.1 has been treated as hostile witnesses and cross-examined by the learned Public Prosecutor.
Nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to prove the case of the prosecution.
Ex.P1 complaint and Ex.P2 Mahazar are not proved by the prosecution.
12.PW.2 Smt. Meena being the victim and wife of the accused deposed that her marriage was solemnized with the accused in the year 2008 at Adichunchanagiri Temple.
It was second marriage to the accused.
The accused had obtained divorce from his first wife.
The accused is working as Driver in BMTC, Bangalore.
They blessed with a daughter.
There was minor matrimonial dispute between her and the accused, as such PW.1 gave an oral complaint to the concerned police to advise the accused to lead happy married life with her.
The accused is now leading happy married life with their daughter.
She did not give any statement to the concerned police alleging that the accused by suspecting her fidelity attempted to stab her.
She denies statement given before the I.O., marked as Ex.P3.
Nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.2 to establish the case of the prosecution.
13.PW.3 H. P. Sharathkumar Police Sub-Inspector, Rajagopalanagar P.S., Bangalore, conducted part of the investigation in this case.
On 11.08.2016 PW.3 visited Rajiv Gandhi Hospital and collected Ex.P4 wound certificate and filed charge sheet against the accused for the alleged offences.

On perusal of Ex.P4 wound certificate it appears that PW.2 Smt. Meena admitted to Tuberculosis Research Center and Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Chest Diseases with history of assault on 6.1.2016 at 9.00 p.m.

entities.text: Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Chest Diseases
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It seems that PW.2 had sustained a grievous injury and admitted to the Hospital with history of assault.
But she deposed in her evidence that Ex.P1 complaint was filed by her sister to advise the accused to lead happy marital life with their daughter.
PW.2 has not deposed anything against the accused as alleged by the prosecution.
Alleged mental and physical harassment or attempt to commit stab injury with knowledge and intention to kill PW.2 has not been proved by the prosecution with available evidence on record.

The witnesses cited in the charge sheet i.e., CW.2,
CW.3, CW.4, CW.5 to CW.7, CW.9, CW.10, and CW.11 to CW.13 are dropped due to non execution of process issued by this Court.
Very complainant and the victim turned hostile to the case of the prosecution.
The prosecution has failed to prove the charge leveled against accused.
Offence alleged to have been committed punishable U/s.498A and 307 of IPC has not been established by the prosecution.
Accordingly, I answer Points No.1 and 2 in the Negative.

14. Point No.3: In view of answer of court on points No.1 to 4, this court pass the following:-
ORDER Acting U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.498A and 307 of IPC .
